rv.q: What we see here is a full-on recreation of the form, thus begging another question: Why not just go and see the real thing?

Christopher Llewyn Ramirez’ and Jeff Colangelo’s 100-minute odyssey through lucha libre — the Mexico-born sport/theater hybrid starring masked fighters with torrid backstories and bone-crunching moves — merges sport with theater with fabulous impact.
This show is truly a must-see experience.
No matter their age or interest in sports, audiences will find themselves inexplicably drawn into this heroic story and the melodramatics of the play.

Those puzzling, penultimate moments ring false and diminish the impact of the coda -- a ritualistic dance involving the passing of a tradition from one generation to the next -- that makes for an unsatisfying conclusion to an otherwise entertaining show.
The ensuing hilarious and decisive battle was so epic that it busted out of the boundaries of the wrestling ring and the theater itself temporarily.
This play is unique and as an audience member, you will find yourself cheering and or booing and in some cases, both.
Nonstop action and larger-than-life characters make for a rip-roaring good time from start to finish.

cn.t: Critics celebrate "Lucha Teotl" as a thoroughly entertaining and unique theatrical experience that successfully brings the spectacle of lucha libre to the stage with exuberant energy and cultural authenticity.
